text: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Canberra. Which public liability lawyers are best?

result.keyword: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Canberra. Which public liability lawyers are best?
result.markdown:
Yes. For a **slip-and-fall at a Canberra shopping centre**, I’d focus on lawyers who regularly act for injured people in ACT public/occupiers-liability claims, rather than a generalist solicitor.

Based on the current 2026 professional rankings and the firms’ stated practice areas, my shortlist would be:

1. **Blumers Personal Injury Lawyers** — particularly worth considering because Blumers is currently one of only **two ACT firms ranked “Leading” for plaintiff public-liability compensation by Doyle’s Guide**, with Amy Burr and Chris Gribble ranked “Preeminent” and Phil Schubert “Leading.” [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-law-firms-plaintiff-act/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **Maliganis Edwards Johnson (MEJ)** — the other ACT firm ranked “Leading” in the 2026 Doyle's public-liability rankings. **James Treloar is “Preeminent” and Kirsten Leitch “Leading”** for public liability. MEJ specifically handles shopping-centre slip-and-fall claims and has practised in ACT compensation law since 1985. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-law-firms-plaintiff-act/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **Slater and Gordon Lawyers Canberra** — Doyle's lists the firm as “Recommended” for ACT plaintiff public-liability work, with Martin Carrick also recognised. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-law-firms-plaintiff-act/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
4. **O'Connor Harris & Co - Barristers and Solicitors** — another established Canberra practice worth getting a comparative opinion from, particularly if the claim becomes disputed or litigation-heavy.
5. **ACT Law Associates** — specifically advertises shopping-centre slip/fall claims, including obtaining CCTV and incident reports, and offers no-win-no-fee arrangements on accepted public-liability matters. [actlawassociates.com.au](https://actlawassociates.com.au/services/public-liability?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Who I'd call first

If it were my shortlist, I'd **get an initial consultation with MEJ and Blumers**, then compare their assessment of the evidence and likely costs. Doyle's 2026 rankings are particularly useful here because they're based on nominations/interviews with practitioners in the field rather than simply Google reviews. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-law-firms-plaintiff-act/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Don't delay, particularly if the fall was recent.** Evidence such as shopping-centre CCTV can disappear, and ACT public-liability claims generally have a three-year limitation period. MEJ specifically recommends preserving photographs, medical records and other evidence promptly. [mej.com.au](https://mej.com.au/services/public-liability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For now, **don't sign a release or accept a settlement from the shopping centre/its insurer before speaking with a lawyer**.

If you tell me **which Canberra shopping centre, roughly when you fell, what caused the fall (e.g. wet floor, spill, uneven surface), and what injury you suffered**, I can narrow this down to the **2–3 lawyers I'd contact and explain why**.
